sections.heading: Vibration energy harvesting using highly (001)-oriented $\mathsf { P b } ( \mathsf { Z r } , \mathsf { T i } ) \mathsf { O } _ { 3 }$ thin film
sections.text:
Takakiyo Harigai,a) Hideaki Adachi, and Eiji Fujii   
Advanced Technology Research Laboratories, Panasonic Corporation, 3-4 Hikaridai, Seika-cho,   
Kyoto 619-0237, Japan

(Received 11 January 2010; accepted 22 March 2010; published online 3 May 2010)

Energy conversion from mechanical vibration into electric power was investigated using the piezoelectric $\mathrm { P b } ( \mathrm { Z r } , \mathrm { T i } ) { \mathrm { O } } _ { 3 }$ lead zirconate titanate (PZT) thin film with highly (001)-orientation. The piezoelectric $d _ { 3 1 }$ constant was found to be as large as $- 1 5 0 \ \mathrm { p C } / \mathrm { N }$ The generated electric voltage under vibration acceleration of $4 5 \mathrm { \ m } / \mathrm { s } ^ { 2 }$ at $2 4 5 0 \mathrm { H z }$ for the PZT/Si cantilever exceeded $2 \mathrm { \Delta V }$ and the operation of light emitting diode lighting was demonstrated. The average output power of $1 0 0 ~ \mu \mathrm { W }$ was obtained at the impedance-matched load resistance of $2 . 2 \ \mathrm { k } \Omega$ . The generated power density of $5 0 \mathrm { ~ \ } \mu \mathrm { W / m m } ^ { 3 }$ was much larger than that of conventional piezoelectric harvesters. $©$ 2010 American Institute of Physics. [doi:10.1063/1.3406253]

The vibration-based energy harvesting are of interest in numerous applications as wireless and self-sustaining microdevices. For the conversion of mechanical vibration energy into electric power, electromagnetic induction, electrostatic induction, and piezoelectricity are commonly used. Among these conversion mechanisms, the piezoelectric transduction is expected for the high power density as its generation structure is much simpler and needs less volume, which is suitable for the power generation of microdevices. Numerous studies concerning the piezoelectric harvester were perormed o the last decadeThe power densiy piezoelectric energy harvesting was ranging around $0 . 0 1 { - } 0 . 5 \ \mu \mathrm { W } / \mathrm { m m } ^ { 3 }$ under the several excitation ratio of mechanical vibration.' For the realization of self-powered microdevices, piezoelectric thin films should be grown on microscopically fabricable substrates such as Si single crystal. Several researches have been reported on the energy harvesting using piezoelectric lead zirconate titanate (PZT) thin films.8-1 In these previous researches, most of PZT thin films were made by sol-gel processes. Muralt et al. successfully fabricated (001)-PZT films on Si substrate and revealed that (001)-films exhibit higher transverse piezoelectric coeffent  h 1m21 It is, therefore, quite interesting to make piezoelectric power generator using highly (001)-oriented PZT thin films with large piezoelectricity.

Recently we have fabricated the cantilever-type energy harvesting devices using highly (001)-oriented piezoelectric PZT thin films on Si substrates and examined their power generation from external mechanical vibration. Since the piezoelectricity of the film strongly depends on the orientation distribution of polar $c$ -axis, large power generation can be expected by using the large piezoelectric PZT thin film. Here we report the basic properties of PZT thin-film energy generator which shows larger power density than conventional one.

Ferroelectric PZT thin film with perovskite structure was prepared by a radio-frequency magnetron sputtering onto heated Si (100) wafer covered by Ir bottom electrode. The thicknesses of the PZT thin film and the Ir electrode were $3 . 6 ~ \mu \mathrm { m }$ and $1 0 0 \ \mathrm { n m }$ ,respectively. A sintered ceramic disk with a composition close to morphotropic phase boundary (MPB) $[ ( \mathrm { P b } \mathrm { Z r } _ { 0 . 5 3 } \mathrm { T i } _ { 0 . 4 7 } \mathrm { O } _ { 3 } ) _ { 0 . 8 } + ( \mathrm { P b } \mathrm { O } ) _ { 0 . 2 } ]$ was used as a sputtering target.14 The (001) orientation of the PZT thin film were strongly dependent on the film growth conditions, especially on the $\mathbf { A r } / \mathbf { O } _ { 2 }$ mixture gas ratio in the sputtering atmosphere. X-ray diffraction (XRD) pattern of the PZT thin film with $3 . 3 \mathrm { - } \mu \mathrm { m }$ -thickness deposited with $1 \%$ $\mathrm { O } _ { 2 }$ mixture gas $\left( \mathrm { A r } / \mathrm { O } _ { 2 } { = } 9 9 / 1 \right.$ ) shows that the film was composed of randomly oriented polycrystalline phase with the perovskite structure [Fig. 1(a)]. By increasing the $\mathrm { ~ O } _ { 2 }$ ratio to $5 \%$ in the mixture gas, the (001)-oriented PZT thin film was obtained. However the surface of the PZT film was changed from transparent to cloudy, which indicates a leakage nature. In order to prepare (001)-oriented and transparent PZT thin films, we carried out two-step deposition. At the first stage, the $0 . 2 \mathrm { - } \mu \mathrm { m }$ -thick PZT film was formed with $5 \%$ $\mathrm { O } _ { 2 }$ mixture gas on $\mathrm { I r } / \mathrm { S i }$ substrate, and then the main PZT film with $3 . 3 \mathrm { - } \mu \mathrm { m }$ -thickness was deposited with $1 \%$ $\mathrm { { O } } _ { 2 }$ atmosphere. Figure 1(b) shows the XRD pattern of the resultant PZT film. The film exhibits highly (001)-preferred orientation $c$ -domain) with the $c$ -axis length of $0 . 4 0 7 ~ \mathrm { n m }$ We found no amount of the other oriented phase of PZT such as (110) or (111) structure. By the present two-step deposition, highly (001)-oriented PZT films with transparent and glossy surface were prepared.

The piezoelectricity of the PZT thin film was measured by fabricating a unimorph cantilever from the as-grown PZT/Si wafer. The rectangular cantilever beam was patterned with standard photolithography and dry etching processes after the evaporation of $2 0 0 \mathrm { - n m \ A u / T i }$ top electrode on the PZT/Si wafer. Dimensions of the cantilever beam were $7 7 0 0 \ \mu \mathrm { m }$ in length, $1 8 0 0 ~ \mu \mathrm { m }$ in width, and $1 2 0 ~ \mu \mathrm { m }$ in thickness. The piezoelectricity of the PZT thin film was evaluated by measuring the deflection at the free end of the cantilever beam with a laser displacement meter against the applied electric voltage between bottom Ir and top Au electrodes. After the deposition, no switching voltage was applied to the PZT thin film. Figure 2 shows the deflection $( \delta )$ versus electric voltage $( V )$ curves of PZT/Si unimorph cantilever. The inset is the schematic illustration of the measurement setup. In the measuring voltage range $( \pm 1 0 \mathrm { ~ V } )$ , linearlike curves with trace amount of hysteresis were observed. From the polarity of the beam bending against the applied voltage, the spontaneous polarization $( P _ { s } )$ of the as-grown PZT thin film was confirmed to arrange orienting from the bottom electrode to the film surface without any poling treatments as shown in this figure. This intrinsically aligned polarization was occasionally observed in $\mathrm { P b }$ -based ferroelectric thin films. The origin could be understood by theidea that the orientation of the polarization was strongly affected by the chemistry of environment at the surface of the film.16 A certain growth atmosphere during the sputtering deposition might determine the direction of $P _ { s }$ in the present PZT thin film. The piezoelectric coefficient $d _ { 3 1 }$ was estimated by the following equation:

where $l$ is the length of the cantilever beam, $t _ { s }$ and $t _ { f }$ are the thicknesses of the Si substrate and PZT film, respectively, and $s _ { s }$ and $s _ { f }$ are the mechanical compliances of the Si substrate and PZT film, respectively. The $d _ { 3 1 }$ value of the present highly (001)-oriented PZT film by two-step deposition process was found to be $- 1 5 0 \ \mathrm { p C } / \mathrm { N }$ ,which was a quite large value compared with other PZT film (the randomoriented film was $- 8 0 \ \mathrm { p C / N ) }$ and bulk PZT of the same composition. The larger piezoelectricity could generate the higher voltage in the energy conversion from mechanical vibration. Moreover, the present intrinsic polarization in the PZT film was great useful as energy harvesting because there is no necessity of poling treatment and no worry concerning the depolarization during energy generation from the mechanical vibration.

Using the PZT/Si unimorph cantilever, energy conversion from the mechanical vibration into electric power was examined. The cantilever beam was mounted on an electromagnetic mechanical shaker and driven at different frequencies. No proof mass was used for the cantilever and the device was oscillated in the out-of-plane direction, same as the gravity. The generated alternate voltage between bottom and top electrodes became maximum at the resonant frequency around $2 4 5 0 ~ \mathrm { ~ H z }$ . Under the vibration acceleration of $4 5 \mathrm { \ m } / \mathrm { s } ^ { 2 }$ the output peak-to-peak voltage $V _ { p - p }$ exceeded $2 \mathrm { V } ,$ which is larger than the threshold voltage of light emitting diode (LED). Demonstration of LED lighting was carried out using the GaAs-based red LED and the rectification diode. Figures 3(a) and 3(b) show the schematic diagram of experimental circuit and the photograph of LED lighting. Frequent lighting operation was verified with no step-up dc-dc converters and no energy storage capacitors as shown in the Fig. 3(b). Using the piezoelectric thin-film power generator, practical operation of electric devices could be presented for the first time.

Power generation properties were measured by connecting the external load resistance between bottom and top electrodes under vibration acceleration of $4 5 \mathrm { \ m } / \mathrm { s } ^ { 2 }$ at $2 4 5 0 ~ \mathrm { H z }$ . The peak-to-peak load voltages $( V _ { p - p } )$ are plotted as a function of load resistance $( R _ { \mathrm { l o a d } } )$ in Fig. 4(a). The open voltage $V _ { p - p } \sim 2$ V lowered with the decrease of $R _ { \mathrm { l o a d } }$ showing the abrupt reduction near $R _ { \mathrm { l o a d } }$ of several kilo-ohms. The generated average power $( P _ { a v e } )$ was estimated by

The maximum output power of $P _ { a v e } { = } 1 0 0 ~ \mu \mathrm { W }$ was obtained at the impedance-matched load resistance of $2 . 2 \ \mathrm { k } \Omega$ .This optimal load resistance corresponds to roughly estimated internal impedance $\left. Z \right. = \left. 1 / j \omega C _ { 0 } \right.$ ,where $\omega$ is the angular frequency and $C _ { 0 }$ is the electrostatic capacity of the cantilever $( 3 5 ~ \mathrm { ~ n F } )$ . The output root mean square current $\left( I _ { r m s } \right)$ was calculated and its relationship with the voltage $( V _ { r m s } )$ is plotted in Fig. 4(b) coincidentally. At the maximum output power, the average current $\left( I _ { r m s } \right)$ reaches more than $2 0 0 ~ \mu \mathrm { A }$ , which is promising for the operation of practical microdevices. The effective volume of the power generator was almost equal to that of cantilever, $2 . 0 \ \mathrm { m m } ^ { 3 }$ . So the generated average power density was estimated to be $5 0 \mathrm { ~ \ } \mu \mathrm { W / m m } ^ { 3 }$ , which was much larger than the conventional piezoelectric harvesting devices. When the rectification diode is used as shown in Fig. 3(b), momentary output power was considered to be eight times $\{ = ( 2 \sqrt { 2 } ) ^ { 2 } \}$ larger than the average power estimated by Eq. (2). This means that the output power of nearly $1 \mathrm { m W }$ is generated in every moment.

The present experiments were carried out without proof mass in order to examine the generation performance and basic properties of the primitive PZT/Si cantilever. The operation frequency and acceleration for the power generation were more than $2 \mathrm { k H z }$ and $4 5 \mathrm { \ m } / \mathrm { s } ^ { 2 }$ respectively, which was higher than that of ambient vibration existing in the environment. The excitation ratio of mechanical vibration defined as $\Omega { = } ( A ^ { 2 } / 8 \pi f )$ was 0.03 in our measurement conditions. This obtained value 0.03 was reasonable standard conditions compared to operating conditions for various energy harvesting devices (see Ref. 7). Using the proof mass at the free end of the cantilever could lead to the decrease of resonant frequency and hereby lowering the operation acceleration, and one can control the resonance frequency to that of the objective vibration source. The finite element (FE) simulation results indicated that the resonance frequency decreased to 500 $\mathrm { H z }$ when the weight of $2 5 ~ \mathrm { m g }$ was mounted in the point of the cantilever.

In summary, large power generation has been achieved using the highly (001)-oriented piezoelectric PZT thin film. The polarization of the PZT film on Si substrate was intrinsically aligned from bottom to top electrode and its piezoelectric $d _ { 3 1 }$ constant was found to be as large as $- 1 5 0 \mathrm { p C } / \mathrm { N }$ which were fairly advantageous for the harvesting from the mechanical vibration. The average output power of $1 0 0 ~ \mu \mathrm { W }$ was obtained at the impedance-matched load resistance of $2 . 2 \ \mathrm { k } \Omega$ The generated power density of $5 0 \mathrm { ~ \ } \mu \mathrm { W / m m } ^ { 3 }$ was much larger than that of conventional piezoelectric harvesters. Since the operation frequency and sensitivity can be controlled by the use of the proof mass, practical power generation from the ambient vibration may be possible. The present large piezoelectric PZT film with highly (001)-orientation has potential advantage in the energy harvesting for microdevices with wireless and self-sustaining operation.
